song_craft: Voice: stotra-address couplets — Abhinavagupta’s own hymn, first person throughout, vocatives load-bearing every verse (row 7). Arc: veneration-by-becoming (v1) → two-step recognition (v2) → fear-denied-suffering-kept (v3) → death defied (v4) → fearlessness finished (v5) → awakening→ingress (v6) → affliction-as-occasion (v7) → rites relativized (v8) → dancing consciousness (v9) → dated seal cooling the world (v10). Recognition performed, not argued. L4 = L3 verbatim, music named.

lines: This consciousness of mine dances, sings, rejoices deeply — O Bhairava, Lord:
having won You, my dear — a single beautiful vision, hard for others to obtain, kept for knowers of the covenant.
l4.sanskrit_cite: nṛtyati gāyati hṛṣyati gāḍham saṃvit iyam mama bhairavanātha tvāṃ priyam āpya sudarśanamekam durlabhamanyajanaiḥ samayajñam
notes: sudarśanam ekam as ‘a single beautiful vision’ (boundary open); samayajñam as qualifier (fence), with C1

verses.craft: Joy first, cause named (obtaining=vision); fence kept (covenant-knowers); samayajña/sudarśanam-ekam opens per NOTE.
verses.rejected: (a) dances→dance-syntax flatten → killed: three verbs dance. (b) resolving fence-address → killed by UNC.
verses.reads: argmap Q+INF (+UNC ["Whether 'samayajña' is vocative or qualifier converging on the same fence is unresolved.", "Whether 'sudarśanam ekam' means 'the one beautiful vision' or 'beautiful vision alone' is unresolved."]) / C1 essence / rasa ānanda (bliss) with adbhuta (wonder) / L2+L3 voice
